Consult Summary:
- Adult male with acute left-sided headache since this morning, suspected tension-type headache versus migraine; advised analgesia, lifestyle measures, counseling referral, and follow-up in one week.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Acute, severe left-sided headache that woke patient at ~05:30 this morning; headache still present at time of consult.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Onset: this morning (woke patient at ~05:30).
  - Course: persistent since onset; described as more severe than his usual headaches.
  - Past headache history: intermittent headaches previously, typically milder and centered at front of the head (not strictly one-sided).
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Worse initially on lying down (takes time to get comfortable).
  - Overall feels better when lying down after initial soreness.
  - Took paracetamol this morning without meaningful relief.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Mild photophobia (lights make eyes a little sore, tolerable).
  - Brief dizziness on waking that has since subsided.
  - No nausea currently.
  - No neck stiffness, no fever.
- Relevant psychosocial factors:
  - Current increased work-related stress for ~2 months with late nights and backlog of work.
  - Reports history of anxiety for ~2 years.
  - Denies current thoughts of self-harm.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives:
  - No fever, no persistent nausea, no neck stiffness, no focal neurologic complaints reported.

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety, approximately 2 years' duration; on treatment with sertraline.
- No other chronic medical conditions reported.
- No history of hypertension; reports never having blood pressure checked.

Medications:
- Sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Paracetamol — taken this morning; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Recommended: Ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented (discussed and advised as first-line for suspected migraine-type headache).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Non-smoker.
- Has a cat at home.
- Exercises: running approximately three times per week.
- Diet: describes as "okay" / not particularly healthy but not unhealthy.
- Alcohol/substance use: not mentioned.
- Occupational stress: significant work-related stress for about two months with late nights; advised possible time off work (self-certify one week).

Family History:
- Mother with history of anxiety.
- No other familial diagnoses of migraines or physical illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person physical examination performed during this consult.
- No vital signs recorded.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results available or performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute headache (differential: tension-type headache vs migraine)
  - Assessment:
    - Acute left-sided headache waking patient from sleep; mild photophobia increases likelihood of migraine, but background of work stress and anxiety supports tension-type headache as alternative.
    - No red-flag features reported (no fever, no neck stiffness, no focal neurologic symptoms reported).
  - Plan:
    - Start ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as first-line analgesic for suspected migraine; may continue paracetamol if desired.
    - Advise rest and consider taking time off work; suggested self-certify for one week.
    - Sleep hygiene: aim for a minimum of 7–8 hours per night.
    - Hydration: aim for 1.5–2.0 liters of fluids per day (excluding coffee/tea).
    - Provide link in notes to headache danger signs and safety information; advised to read.
    - Follow-up arranged in one week; earlier contact if symptoms worsen or new concerning features develop.
    - If not improving, consider blood tests or further evaluation / imaging as appropriate on follow-up.

- Issue 2: Anxiety (chronic)
  - Assessment:
    - Ongoing anxiety managed with sertraline; contributing factor to current stress and possible tension-type headache.
    - No current suicidal ideation.
  - Plan:
    - Continue sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Recommend counseling / psychological support; clinician to include self-referral link to local counseling service in notes.

- General plan items:
  - Safety netting: patient advised to seek earlier review if symptoms worsen or new concerning features occur.
  - Follow-up appointment scheduled in one week with clinician or another GP.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature).
  - Formal physical and neurological examination findings.
  - Pain severity score.
  - Exact doses, routes, and frequencies for sertraline, paracetamol, and recommended ibuprofen.
  - Any prior headache workup or imaging history.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Transcript clear and audible; information sufficient for history and plan but no objective examination data recorded.
